raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

SGLang supports I-quant GGUF weights for dequantization and MMVQ, but does not
currently include them in dense or batched-MoE MMQ dispatch. Beyond the
small-batch MMVQ boundary, dense I-quant prefill dequantizes the full weight to
BF16, while I-quant MoE prefill remains on the decode-oriented vector kernel.

This change adds the eight I-quant formats supported by the upstream MMQ
implementation. `IQ1_M` remains on fallback because that implementation does
not provide its MMQ dot product.

Fixes #35019

## Modifications

- Add CUDA dense and batched-MoE MMQ support for `IQ1_S`, `IQ2_XXS`,
  `IQ2_XS`, `IQ2_S`, `IQ3_XXS`, `IQ3_S`, `IQ4_NL`, and `IQ4_XS`.
- Apply a conservative M<=16 IQ MMQ gate. Wide matrices use MMVQ through M=8,
  MMQ for M=9..16, and dequantization from M=17. Narrow matrices retain MMVQ
  through M=16 and dequantization from M=17.
- Route pure or mixed IQ MoE to batched MMQ from M=128 only when assignment
  reuse, expert count, CUDA grid capacity, and both projection K alignments are
  suitable.
- Add an AOT capability query and enable IQ MMQ in SRT only when the installed
  `sglang-kernel` exposes that capability.
- Reject unsupported `Q8_1` in the high-level selector and direct CUDA GGUF
  compute entry points.
- Harden shared MoE contracts with scalar catch-all registration, 64-bit expert
  strides, padded-tail bounds, complete q8 scale-tile loading, low-level
  alignment checks, and deterministic zero output for invalid or remote
  experts.
- Add registered CPU routing tests, CUDA dense and pure/mixed MoE regression
  coverage, and a checked-in dense benchmark using a revision-pinned GGUF
  fixture.

The SRT caller enables IQ MMQ only when its loaded kernel package exposes the
new capability; otherwise it retains the vector/dequantization fallback. The
historical compatibility tests below used `sglang-kernel==0.4.6.post1`.
At the current PR head and the latest tested main, the dependency pins have
advanced to `sglang-kernel==0.4.9` and `torch==2.14.1`. A kernel release
containing the new capability and a follow-up pin update are still needed to
enable IQ MMQ in normal installations. This PR does not set an unreleased pin.

The kernel implementation is adapted from
`aimbit-ni/vllm@037e1d547c15313aa7e2bb5fc83390ab0c857314` and the algorithms
in `ggml-org/llama.cpp#8495`. `THIRDPARTYNOTICES.txt` includes the ggml MIT
notice.

## Accuracy Tests

### Shared activation-policy revalidation, 2026-10-13

Latest tested main `7ff3a112846a3fcc12a27bba09d644885a226e4d` (#43236)
enables `--use_fast_math` on Blackwell in the shared activation called by
GGUF MoE. I tested main and a clean detached merge with the unchanged PR head
`0a39ec3a8754e3c4426950a5a93046c048a03f07`; the integration tree is
`36909c6658f0ce1ed346db5b85a3568325b9357d`, still 15 files (+4127/-81).
The original PR branch was not rewritten or advanced for this verification.

[Pinned report with raw logs, compiler invocations and reproduction scripts](https://github.com/liuhao-labs/sglang/tree/60c31a451ad6bd2db607a655b1c9724cd320e0a2/36122/activation-math-20261013)

- Separate cold-cache precise/fast-math builds: 60 activation comparisons on
  main and 60 on main+PR, all finite and within existing `0.01/0.01` bounds.
- Real two-projection GGUF + shared default JIT activation: 160 cases on each
  source, covering FP16/BF16, SiLU/GELU, eight IQ types, mixed Q5_0 directions
  and M=1/127/128/129. Fast-vs-precise max difference: `3.05176e-5`.
- Registered routing CPU suite: 10 passed; registered activation subset:
  54 passed; existing GGUF AOT module: 153 passed. Four main+PR full MoE
  CUDA Graph replays match eager outputs exactly.

The component checks use Torch 2.11/CUDA13, newly compiled GGUF functions in an
isolated test namespace and the recorded auxiliary 0.4.4 wheel. They do not
prove the PR-built full wheel's ABI. No numerical kernel is mocked.

I then resolved the cached-image gap using the official hash-verified
`sglang-kernel 0.4.9` wheel with matched Torch 2.14.1, Transformers 5.19.0,
FlashInfer 0.7.1, CUTLASS DSL 4.8.0 and Triton 3.8.0 in a separate environment.
The unmodified published wheel loaded successfully (SHA256
`384a0d2158740f5ab42cfc64c872640bb3c80f3b0ec3b4666bc3efb553254bc4`).
Both pinned main and main+PR loaded the exact prior 0.5B IQ3_S GGUF model and
returned health/generate HTTP 200, 8 prompt / 16 completion tokens, zero
cached tokens, and identical output token IDs/text. The canonical output hash
is `2604448b1bc1b2c9a10961f6b562bed70aab5041db4cb8a7db54e83f9cfde287`.
[Paired serving provenance, raw logs and comparison](https://github.com/liuhao-labs/sglang/tree/3bba28741dd6b7e39466e8f540b3e7ffc7703ef9/36122/activation-math-20261013/runtime-049)
No test-namespace operator replacement or version-check bypass was used in
these serving runs; capability is false with the published wheel.

This proves the current released-wheel small dense-model fallback/serving path,
not enabled IQ MMQ full-model serving or the PR-built full wheel's ABI. Official
CI and H100/B200 remain separate requirements. The first 0.03 memory-fraction
attempt hit the real KV budget guard, so both final arms used 0.05, the same
1024-token cap, one request and a 10 GiB container limit. No PR-related
numerical regression or required feature-code change was found.

### Published MoE binding follow-up, 2026-10-13

I additionally tested latest main
`27b68303d043ddbddf9861c55c26bc8617ea7c35` and its clean detached merge with
this PR (`449c32e493e80e67190fcf1f61976dc6045159e9`, tree
`bb5c83cc334e80c51e6a0eb44045a5358c189162`) using the **unmodified official
0.4.9 production common_ops** and Torch 2.14.1/CUDA13. Each source passed
32 real two-projection expert-layer cases: eight IQ formats, FP16/BF16,
SiLU/GELU, M=128/E=8/top-k=2, input/intermediate width 256. Outputs were
finite and within `atol=1, rtol=0.1` of the dequantized reference; maximum
absolute error was 0.00366211. All 32 paired outputs were bit-identical.
Profiler records two real `sgl_kernel::ggml_moe_a8_vec` calls and the shared
default fast-math activation; fresh caches and actual compiler flags were
recorded. Capability remains false, so this is released-wheel expert-layer
fallback validation, not enabled IQ MMQ or full expert-model serving.

[Raw outputs, library hashes, compiler commands and build attempts](https://github.com/liuhao-labs/sglang/tree/51499c19cc3ec4e8bd6d6b3c4e64d807f5d6c4e5/36122/activation-math-20261013/production-bindings-followup)

I attempted the complete current-source AOT wheel with matched Torch and
one build worker/NVCC thread. Default builds hit cgroup OOM at 10 and 14 GiB
in existing FP8 units; an all-source/all-default-target build with SM121a-only
common_ops also hit 14 GiB OOM in the same existing `fp8_gemm_kernel.cu`.
Those failing source units are identical on latest main and main+PR.
Commands, exit 137, three Docker OOM events and resource samples are included.
No wheel was emitted: the prepared 80 enabled-production cases and 153-test
GGUF run against a new full wheel were **not executed**. New full-wheel ABI,
capability=true expert validation and official H100/B200 CI remain outstanding.
The earlier component/test-namespace passes do not fill these gaps.

The 15 upstream commits since the earlier frozen main did not change GGUF,
shared activation/JIT core or AOT build metadata by blob. The clean merge
still has the same 15-file feature diff; the original PR head was not rewritten.
Latest main and official 0.4.9 still lack IQ-MMQ capability, so the proposed
support remains necessary. This follow-up is correctness/build evidence;
historical speed figures below retain their original pinned runtime.

### Historical pinned-runtime validation

Local validation used the installed CUDA 13/aarch64 AOT wheel on one NVIDIA
GB10 (`sm_121`), rather than JIT-compiled kernels.

The prior validation used upstream base
`0c84eaba7f8d6674a360839426cacde4e1acd851` and clean local head
`4c3e4c2350f4d6c4ff2a785e9b294938766a3cc6`. On 2026-10-09, upstream `main`
was synchronized through `6e7beace143964386ce2e4418401b7369f0dabd0` into the
current PR head `0a39ec3a8754e3c4426950a5a93046c048a03f07`. The three-way merge
was clean and the feature diff remains exactly 15 files (+4127/-81). The 67
intervening main commits have no path overlap with the feature files; the four
overlapping paths from the earlier sync contained only AOT cleanup and
formatting, not GGUF MMQ logic. The local numbers below belong to the historical
validation head and runtime; they do not validate the current upstream runtime
end to end. The refreshed head is pending official CI.

- historical validated wheel SHA-256:
  `626d6ee79dd37dae2242f2f18a97b0536c95dfa4c053cb56d7573de23324c6e0`
- registered CPU routing and compatibility suite: `10 passed`
- patch-focused GGUF CUDA matrix: `57 passed`
- complete `python/sglang/kernels/aot/tests/test_gguf.py`:
  `153 passed`
- installed-wheel production smoke: passed

Using the same CUDA 13/aarch64 build configuration, the compressed wheel grew
from 29.473 MiB to 30.999 MiB: +1.527 MiB (+5.18%). Each bundled
architecture-specific `common_ops` shared object grew by 917,504 bytes.

The historical wheel was built before the August main-only merge. Its AOT tree,
SRT GGUF selector and registered routing test matched the August validation head
`4c3e4c2350f4d6c4ff2a785e9b294938766a3cc6`. That source-equivalence statement
does not extend to the October runtime or today's shared activation policy.

The production smoke observed the new capability as enabled and covered:

- wide dense IQ MMQ at M=16 and dequantization fallback at M=17
- exact fixed-shape CUDA Graph capture/replay
- MoE vector dispatch at M=127 and batched dispatch at M=128
- pure and mixed quantization at M=128, M=256, and M=2050
- `Q8_1` rejection, K-alignment guards, and invalid-expert zero output

Maximum reserved GPU memory during the production smoke was 528 MiB.

A compatibility smoke combined the patched SRT source with a locally cached
`sglang-kernel==0.4.6.post1` baseline artifact (SHA-256
`c7aac3ab20ff3c704e2bbc1a2fa78e5142a65150f12bca74f8e4cbd4f651d958`). This is
not the published PyPI artifact. The published aarch64 wheel has SHA-256
`7eccd61408b44b55ab35cdbcf8a05243ce2a9a5e781fabb00da375af7d7130a1`; the
external 4k run below used that published wheel. The local smoke observed
`capability=False`, selected `dequantize` for an IQ dense input, and returned
shape `[9, 18944]`. This verifies that the combined source remains correct
before the new kernel wheel is released.

A final-head bounded end-to-end serving sanity check also passed with the
artifacts in `/tmp/sglang-36122-e2e-final.XwQYAu` and the revision-pinned
[`legraphista/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-IMat-GGUF`](https://huggingface.co/legraphista/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-IMat-GGUF/tree/7964190b472f46504534873d2cc148510e3e3f34)
`Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct.IQ3_S.gguf` file (SHA-256
`b7685f565fc6e49a8f9bc0fe09b9bb22ca0d5e4b10635cd4b181597f113794b6`).
The installed patch wheel (SHA-256 `626d6ee7...`) reported `capability=True`;
the same synced SRT with the local baseline artifact (SHA-256 `c7aac3ab...`)
reported `capability=False`. Both configurations loaded the model, returned
HTTP 200 from the health and generation requests, and recorded zero cached
tokens for generation. Their client JSON files were byte-for-byte identical
with SHA-256
`bd3c11d390f7a373e534f5361807119b2c040bc325cfe1f6fd2c8165d4426933`:
11 prompt tokens, 16 completion tokens, a length finish, and text:

```text
 I like to work outside because it is a great way to get exercise. I
```

Both runs used a single GB10 (`sm_121`, CUDA 13, aarch64), read-only source,
wheel, and model mounts, no network or host port, a 10 GiB container memory
limit, `--mem-fraction-static 0.03`, `--max-total-tokens 1024`, one running
request, Triton attention, PyTorch sampling, and CUDA graphs disabled. The patch
run loaded 0.88 GB of weights and allocated approximately 0.02 GB of KV cache.
This validates a small dense IQ3_S model and the released-wheel fallback; it
does not replace testing the original approximately 100 GB routed-expert model.
The critical server-log scan found no traceback, CUDA error, NaN, or
illegal-memory failure; the remaining messages were the expected `nvidia-smi`
fallback and shared local-tokenizer warnings.

The H-specific [Lint workflow](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32939744957)
passed, including the repository pre-commit checks, documentation checks, and
the dedicated sgl-kernel clang-format check. The older
[Lint workflow](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32682791204)
also passed for prior head `0137a1e...`. Normal platform CI is gated on the
repository's `run-ci` label.

The complete local AOT collection is not claimed as passing. A bounded run
reached 971 passed and 2 skipped before an unrelated large AWQ parameter
exceeded the allocator cap. Excluding AWQ reached 970 passed and 2,310 skipped
before FlashMLA sparse prefill rejected SM121.

Normal/full PR CI is still pending because the repository's required `run-ci`
label has not yet been added. The current red PR Test entries are gate failures
for that missing label, and their wheel, H100, and B200 jobs were skipped; they
are not kernel test failures. A maintainer must add `run-ci` (or run the
project's authorized slash command) so the normal workflow builds and installs
the PR-local wheel on the official x86_64/aarch64 and H100/B200 environments.

The Issue reporter subsequently completed a frozen 4k cold-prefill comparison
on this H-pinned source using a reconstructed approximately 99.18 GiB
DeepSeek-V4-Flash 0731 checkpoint ([report](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36122#issuecomment-5428479426),
[follow-up](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36122#issuecomment-5428566143)).
The checkpoint is a reconstruction from surviving Unsloth shards rather than a
bit-identical copy of the deleted original: two MXFP4 expert tensors were
converted to Q8_0 and the remaining tensors were byte-copied. The H source with
the published released aarch64 wheel selected the vector MoE path, while H with
the H-built wheel selected batched MMQ at M>=128; both arms used the same H
source and passed the route and correctness checks.

Across three measured 4k runs (concurrency 1, cold prefill), prefill throughput
was 60.93 versus 97.37 tokens/s (+59.8%), TTFT was 26,513 versus 15,912 ms
(-40.0%), and decode TPOT was 61.60 versus 62.09 ms (+0.8%). The literal U plus
released-wheel arm was not run separately; the reporter's historical 0.5.18
baseline reproduced the issue-scale result. A 16k run was not feasible under
the frozen approximately 99 GiB model and 121 GiB unified-memory budget because
the 4k run left only about 2-3 GiB for KV growth. The reconstructed model also
required an out-of-tree loader patch, so these numbers are targeted external
validation, not an official full-main serving result.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

These are directional route-selection microbenchmarks from a shared GB10 that
retained a live Qwen service. They are not uncontended end-to-end throughput or
cross-architecture claims. They predate the main sync and were not rerun; the
sync did not change the IQ kernel patch represented by these measurements.

The checked-in benchmark compares direct MMQ with dequantization plus BF16
matmul using revision-pinned `18944x1024` GGUF fixtures. The table below uses
two independent benchmark invocations. Each value is the mean speedup, with the
two-run range in brackets; speedup is `(dequantize + BF16 matmul) / MMQ`.

| quant type | M=16 speedup, mean [range] |
|---|---:|
| IQ1_S | 1.75x [1.75x, 1.76x] |
| IQ2_XXS | 1.31x [1.29x, 1.33x] |
| IQ2_XS | 1.26x [1.26x, 1.26x] |
| IQ2_S | 1.60x [1.59x, 1.61x] |
| IQ3_XXS | 1.71x [1.67x, 1.74x] |
| IQ3_S | 1.66x [1.65x, 1.67x] |
| IQ4_NL | 1.48x [1.47x, 1.48x] |
| IQ4_XS | 1.26x [1.24x, 1.28x] |

The full M=9/16/17/24/32 matrix and reproduction notes are in the
[benchmark comment](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36122#issuecomment-5390200192).
The M=16 ranges retain at least 1.24x measured headroom across all eight
formats. Although the isolated M=17 sample was also faster, M=18..23 were not
measured and M=24 regressed on multiple formats. The shared GB10 measurements
do not justify interpolating a larger universal CUDA gate, so this PR uses the
conservative M<=16 boundary. M=17 and above retain dequantization.

Directional MoE measurements were:

| path | vector baseline | batched MMQ | speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| IQ3_S/Q5_0 M=128 | 2.249 ms | 1.490 ms | 1.51x |
| Q5_0/IQ3_S M=128 | 2.524 ms | 1.571 ms | 1.61x |
| IQ3_S/Q5_0 M=256 | 4.497 ms | 1.758 ms | 2.56x |
| Q5_0/IQ3_S M=256 | 5.145 ms | 2.283 ms | 2.25x |
| IQ3_S/Q5_0 M=2050 | 34.801 ms | 9.056 ms | 3.84x |

The external 4k result above is a targeted serving throughput validation; it is
not a claim about uncontended throughput or a literal bit-identical checkpoint.
The 16k comparison and a separately measured literal-U arm remain unavailable
under the reported hardware/model constraints. Official x86_64/aarch64,
H100/B200 CI and maintainer review are still pending; see the
[original reviewer response](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/35019#issuecomment-5414670611)
and the
[pinned U/H protocol](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/35019#issuecomment-5421830355).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (N/A: this changes internal CUDA dispatch without adding a user-facing flag or supported format; the in-tree benchmark and third-party notice were updated.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

### GB10 dense IQ MMQ crossover

![GGUF IQ MMQ crossover on GB10](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/liuhao-labs/sglang/753edaf202cf30a89f0c1d7b43590f5bd4847c4e/36122/dense-crossover-heatmap.png)

This plot uses the revision-pinned `18944x1024` GGUF fixtures on CUDA 13 / GB10
(`sm_121`). Each cell is the mean speedup from two independent invocations of
the checked-in benchmark, with the two-run range shown below it. Speedup is
`(dequantize + BF16 matmul) / MMQ`.

At the sampled MMQ boundary M=16, the two-run ranges retain at least `1.24x`
measured headroom across all eight formats. The isolated M=17 sample was also
faster, but M=18..23 were not measured and M=24 regressed on multiple formats.
To avoid interpolating a universal CUDA threshold from one shared GB10, the PR
uses the conservative M<=16 gate; M=17 and above remain on dequantization.

Run the underlying benchmark twice from `python/sglang/kernels/aot` in an
environment with the current PR wheel installed. The `--local-files-only` flag
requires the pinned fixtures to already be present in the Hugging Face cache;
omit it on the first run if the environment has network access.

```bash
for run in 1 2; do
  python benchmark/bench_gguf_mmq.py \
    --batch-sizes 9,16,17,24,32 \
    --shape 18944x1024 \
    --local-files-only | tee "/tmp/gguf-mmq-run-${run}.md"
done
```

The heatmap was rendered from those two benchmark tables; the plotting-only
helper is not part of this PR. These are directional local microbenchmarks on a
shared GB10 with a live Qwen service, not uncontended end-to-end throughput or
cross-architecture results.

### Additional end-to-end compatibility check

I ran the revision-pinned
[`legraphista/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-IMat-GGUF`](https://huggingface.co/legraphista/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-IMat-GGUF/tree/7964190b472f46504534873d2cc148510e3e3f34)
`Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct.IQ3_S.gguf` file (SHA-256
`b7685f565fc6e49a8f9bc0fe09b9bb22ca0d5e4b10635cd4b181597f113794b6`)
through SGLang's real `/generate` endpoint on a GB10 (`sm_121`, CUDA 13,
aarch64).

| configuration | capability | prompt/completion tokens | result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| patched SRT + PR-local wheel (`dae0fcc2...`) | `true` | 11 / 16 | pass |
| patched SRT + released `sglang-kernel==0.4.6.post1` (`c7aac3ab...`) | `false` | 11 / 16 | pass |

Both greedy requests produced byte-for-byte identical output:

```text
 I like to work outside because it is a great way to get exercise. I
```

The runs used read-only source/wheel/model mounts, no network or host port, a
10 GiB container limit, `--mem-fraction-static 0.03`,
`--max-total-tokens 1024`, one running request, Triton attention, PyTorch
sampling, and disabled CUDA graphs. The patch run loaded 0.88 GB of weights and
allocated approximately 0.02 GB of KV cache.

This is a small dense IQ3_S serving and released-wheel fallback check. It does
not claim end-to-end coverage of the original approximately 100 GB
routed-expert model; pure and mixed MoE paths are covered by the focused CUDA
and installed-wheel production tests described in the PR body.

### Refreshed-head validation

The Draft branch is now synchronized and pinned to:

- `U = 0c84eaba7f8d6674a360839426cacde4e1acd851` — upstream `main` snapshot used as the validation baseline
- `H = 4c3e4c2350f4d6c4ff2a785e9b294938766a3cc6` — current Draft PR head; this merge commit contains `U`

The feature diff from `U` to `H` remains 15 files (`+4127/-81`). The CUDA 13/aarch64 wheel SHA-256 is `626d6ee79dd37dae2242f2f18a97b0536c95dfa4c053cb56d7573de23324c6e0` (30.999 MiB). The wheel-build head and `H` have identical AOT tree, SRT GGUF selector, and registered routing-test Git objects; the final merge only incorporated upstream changes outside those validated surfaces.

Validation on one GB10 (`sm_121`, CUDA 13, aarch64):

- registered CPU routing/compatibility: `10 passed`
- focused GGUF CUDA matrix: `57 passed, 5 warnings in 49.07s`
- complete `test_gguf.py`: `153 passed, 5 warnings in 60.32s`
- installed-wheel production smoke: passed with a 0.06 allocator cap (528 MiB maximum reserved)
  - dense M=16 -> `sgl_kernel::ggml_mul_mat_a8`
  - dense M=17 -> `sgl_kernel::ggml_dequantize`
  - MoE M=127 -> `sgl_kernel::ggml_moe_a8_vec`
  - MoE M=128 and M=2050 -> `sgl_kernel::ggml_moe_a8`
  - fixed-shape CUDA Graph capture/replay matched exactly

I also reran the small revision-pinned IQ3_S serving check on `H` with two kernel-wheel pairings:

| pairing | capability | health/generate | cached prompt tokens | result |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|

| `H` source + released `sglang-kernel==0.4.6.post1` (`c7aac3ab...`) | `false` | 200 / 200 | 0 | pass |

**Arm 2** — H + released wheel:
```
ggml_supports_iq_mmq   -> ABSENT (ImportError)
_supports_iq_mmq        = False
IQ3_XXS in MMQ_QUANT_TYPES = False
MoE   M=1..16384       -> ggml_moe_a8_vec (per-token vec)
dense M>=17            -> dequantize
```

**Arm 3** — H + wheel built from H:
```
ggml_supports_iq_mmq() -> True
_supports_iq_mmq        = True
IQ3_XXS in MMQ_QUANT_TYPES = True
MoE   M=1,8,64,127     -> ggml_moe_a8_vec
```

detail.body:
## Motivation

SGLang supports I-quant GGUF weights for dequantization and MMVQ, but does not
currently include them in dense or batched-MoE MMQ dispatch. Beyond the
small-batch MMVQ boundary, dense I-quant prefill dequantizes the full weight to
BF16, while I-quant MoE prefill remains on the decode-oriented vector kernel.

This change adds the eight I-quant formats supported by the upstream MMQ
implementation. `IQ1_M` remains on fallback because that implementation does
not provide its MMQ dot product.

Fixes #35019

## Modifications

- Add CUDA dense and batched-MoE MMQ support for `IQ1_S`, `IQ2_XXS`,
  `IQ2_XS`, `IQ2_S`, `IQ3_XXS`, `IQ3_S`, `IQ4_NL`, and `IQ4_XS`.
- Apply a conservative M<=16 IQ MMQ gate. Wide matrices use MMVQ through M=8,
  MMQ for M=9..16, and dequantization from M=17. Narrow matrices retain MMVQ
  through M=16 and dequantization from M=17.
- Route pure or mixed IQ MoE to batched MMQ from M=128 only when assignment
  reuse, expert count, CUDA grid capacity, and both projection K alignments are
  suitable.
- Add an AOT capability query and enable IQ MMQ in SRT only when the installed
  `sglang-kernel` exposes that capability.
- Reject unsupported `Q8_1` in the high-level selector and direct CUDA GGUF
  compute entry points.
- Harden shared MoE contracts with scalar catch-all registration, 64-bit expert
  strides, padded-tail bounds, complete q8 scale-tile loading, low-level
  alignment checks, and deterministic zero output for invalid or remote
  experts.
- Add registered CPU routing tests, CUDA dense and pure/mixed MoE regression
  coverage, and a checked-in dense benchmark using a revision-pinned GGUF
  fixture.

The SRT caller enables IQ MMQ only when its loaded kernel package exposes the
new capability; otherwise it retains the vector/dequantization fallback. The
historical compatibility tests below used `sglang-kernel==0.4.6.post1`.
At the current PR head and the latest tested main, the dependency pins have
advanced to `sglang-kernel==0.4.9` and `torch==2.14.1`. A kernel release
containing the new capability and a follow-up pin update are still needed to
enable IQ MMQ in normal installations. This PR does not set an unreleased pin.

The kernel implementation is adapted from
`aimbit-ni/vllm@037e1d547c15313aa7e2bb5fc83390ab0c857314` and the algorithms
in `ggml-org/llama.cpp#8495`. `THIRDPARTYNOTICES.txt` includes the ggml MIT
notice.

## Accuracy Tests

### Shared activation-policy revalidation, 2026-10-13

Latest tested main `7ff3a112846a3fcc12a27bba09d644885a226e4d` (#43236)
enables `--use_fast_math` on Blackwell in the shared activation called by

`0a39ec3a8754e3c4426950a5a93046c048a03f07`; the integration tree is

- Real two-projection GGUF + shared default JIT activation: 160 cases on each
  source, covering FP16/BF16, SiLU/GELU, eight IQ types, mixed Q5_0 directions
  and M=1/127/128/129. Fast-vs-precise max difference: `3.05176e-5`.
- Registered routing CPU suite: 10 passed; registered activation subset:
  54 passed; existing GGUF AOT module: 153 passed. Four main+PR full MoE
  CUDA Graph replays match eager outputs exactly.

The component checks use Torch 2.11/CUDA13, newly compiled GGUF functions in an
isolated test namespace and the recorded auxiliary 0.4.4 wheel. They do not
prove the PR-built full wheel's ABI. No numerical kernel is mocked.

I then resolved the cached-image gap using the official hash-verified
`sglang-kernel 0.4.9` wheel with matched Torch 2.14.1, Transformers 5.19.0,
FlashInfer 0.7.1, CUTLASS DSL 4.8.0 and Triton 3.8.0 in a separate environment.

`384a0d2158740f5ab42cfc64c872640bb3c80f3b0ec3b4666bc3efb553254bc4`).

+"""Benchmark GGUF I-quant dense MMQ against dequantize plus matmul."""
+
+import argparse
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import torch
+import triton.testing
+from gguf import GGMLQuantizationType, GGUFReader
+from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download
+from sgl_kernel import ggml_dequantize, ggml_mul_mat_a8
+
+from sglang.utils import is_in_ci
+
+REPO_ID = "Isotr0py/test-gguf-sample"
+REVISION = "d82b8773934ef260d8d8a896a7c197bc69a0fac1"
+IQ_MMQ_TYPES = (
+    "IQ1_S",
+    "IQ2_XXS",
+    "IQ2_XS",
+    "IQ2_S",
+    "IQ3_XXS",
+    "IQ3_S",
+    "IQ4_NL",
+    "IQ4_XS",
+)
+
+
+def parse_csv(value: str) -> list[str]:
+    return [item.strip() for item in value.split(",") if item.strip()]
+
+
+def parse_int_csv(value: str) -> list[int]:
+    return [int(item) for item in parse_csv(value)]
+
+
+def parse_shape(value: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
+    rows, columns = value.lower().split("x", maxsplit=1)
+    return int(rows), int(columns)
+
+
+def load_quantized_weight(
+    quant_type: GGMLQuantizationType,
+    rows: int,
+    columns: int,
+    *,
+    local_files_only: bool,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    filename = f"Quant_{quant_type.name}_{columns}.gguf"
+    path = hf_hub_download(
+        repo_id=REPO_ID,
+        filename=filename,
+        revision=REVISION,
+        local_files_only=local_files_only,
+    )
+    matches = []
+    for tensor in GGUFReader(Path(path)).tensors:
+        shape = tuple(int(item) for item in tensor.name.rsplit("_", 1)[-1].split("x"))
+        if shape == (rows, columns):
+            matches.append(tensor)
+    if len(matches) != 1:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"expected one {quant_type.name} tensor with shape "
+            f"{rows}x{columns}, found {len(matches)}"
+        )
+    return torch.tensor(matches[0].data, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
+
+
+def benchmark_case(
+    quant_type: GGMLQuantizationType,
+    rows: int,
+    columns: int,
+    batch_size: int,
+    *,
+    local_files_only: bool,
+) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    qweight = load_quantized_weight(
+        quant_type,
+        rows,
+        columns,
+        local_files_only=local_files_only,
+    )
+    x = torch.randn((batch_size, columns), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+
+    def run_mmq() -> torch.Tensor:
+        return ggml_mul_mat_a8(qweight, x, quant_type, rows)
+
+    def run_fallback() -> torch.Tensor:
+        weight = ggml_dequantize(qweight, quant_type, rows, columns, torch.bfloat16)
+        return x @ weight.T
+
+    torch.testing.assert_close(run_mmq(), run_fallback(), atol=1.5, rtol=0.1)
+    quantiles = [0.5, 0.2, 0.8]
+    mmq_ms, _, _ = triton.testing.do_bench_cudagraph(run_mmq, quantiles=quantiles)
+    fallback_ms, _, _ = triton.testing.do_bench_cudagraph(
+        run_fallback, quantiles=quantiles
+    )
+    return mmq_ms, fallback_ms, fallback_ms / mmq_ms
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    is_ci = is_in_ci()
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--quant-types",
+        type=parse_csv,
+        default=["IQ3_S"] if is_ci else list(IQ_MMQ_TYPES),
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--batch-sizes",
+        type=parse_int_csv,
+        default=[16] if is_ci else [9, 16, 17, 24, 32, 64],
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--shape", type=parse_shape, default=(18944, 1024))
+    parser.add_argument("--local-files-only", action="store_true")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+

### GB10 dense IQ MMQ crossover

![GGUF IQ MMQ crossover on GB10](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/liuhao-labs/sglang/753edaf202cf30a89f0c1d7b43590f5bd4847c4e/36122/dense-crossover-heatmap.png)

This plot uses the revision-pinned `18944x1024` GGUF fixtures on CUDA 13 / GB10
(`sm_121`). Each cell is the mean speedup from two independent invocations of
the checked-in benchmark, with the two-run range shown below it. Speedup is
`(dequantize + BF16 matmul) / MMQ`.

At the sampled MMQ boundary M=16, the two-run ranges retain at least `1.24x`
measured headroom across all eight formats. The isolated M=17 sample was also
faster, but M=18..23 were not measured and M=24 regressed on multiple formats.
To avoid interpolating a universal CUDA threshold from one shared GB10, the PR
uses the conservative M<=16 gate; M=17 and above remain on dequantization.

Run the underlying benchmark twice from `python/sglang/kernels/aot` in an
environment with the current PR wheel installed. The `--local-files-only` flag
requires the pinned fixtures to already be present in the Hugging Face cache;
omit it on the first run if the environment has network access.

```bash
for run in 1 2; do
  python benchmark/bench_gguf_mmq.py \
    --batch-sizes 9,16,17,24,32 \
    --shape 18944x1024 \
    --local-files-only | tee "/tmp/gguf-mmq-run-${run}.md"
done
```

The heatmap was rendered from those two benchmark tables; the plotting-only
helper is not part of this PR. These are directional local microbenchmarks on a
shared GB10 with a live Qwen service, not uncontended end-to-end throughput or
cross-architecture results.

### Additional end-to-end compatibility check

I ran the revision-pinned
[`legraphista/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-IMat-GGUF`](https://huggingface.co/legraphista/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-IMat-GGUF/tree/7964190b472f46504534873d2cc148510e3e3f34)
`Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct.IQ3_S.gguf` file (SHA-256
`b7685f565fc6e49a8f9bc0fe09b9bb22ca0d5e4b10635cd4b181597f113794b6`)
through SGLang's real `/generate` endpoint on a GB10 (`sm_121`, CUDA 13,
aarch64).

| configuration | capability | prompt/completion tokens | result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| patched SRT + PR-local wheel (`dae0fcc2...`) | `true` | 11 / 16 | pass |
| patched SRT + released `sglang-kernel==0.4.6.post1` (`c7aac3ab...`) | `false` | 11 / 16 | pass |

Both greedy requests produced byte-for-byte identical output:

```text

```

The runs used read-only source/wheel/model mounts, no network or host port, a
10 GiB container limit, `--mem-fraction-static 0.03`,
`--max-total-tokens 1024`, one running request, Triton attention, PyTorch
sampling, and disabled CUDA graphs. The patch run loaded 0.88 GB of weights and

This is a small dense IQ3_S serving and released-wheel fallback check. It does
not claim end-to-end coverage of the original approximately 100 GB
routed-expert model; pure and mixed MoE paths are covered by the focused CUDA
and installed-wheel production tests described in the PR body.

The Draft branch is now synchronized and pinned to:

## Model

The exact GGUF behind the issue's numbers had been deleted from disk. I reconstructed it from the surviving Unsloth UD-IQ3_XXS shards: the two MXFP4 routed-expert tensors (`blk.26`/`blk.42` `.ffn_down_exps.weight`) converted to Q8_0, every other tensor copied byte-for-byte. 1328 tensors · 99.18 GiB · sha256 17f57289e0d41f913ada93132b645e0920029391f1b3d973b3e5356840c49988

Arms 2 and 3 share an **identical** SGLang source tree — only the kernel wheel differs.

| baseline repro | original issue image `sglang 0.5.18.dev564+gbe804c1b8` + its released kernel | — | released | symbol absent |

| 3 (core) | H | `4c3e4c2350f4…` | built from H checkout (`95cd2ccd…`, 32 521 894 B / 31.01 MiB) | **True** |

If you want the literal U-arm as well I can add it, but it does not change the kernel comparison — arms 2 vs 3 are the isolated pair.

## Route evidence (not the capability flag)

The capability boolean is insufficient on its own, so the PR's own dispatch functions were called from the **installed** wheel against the **installed** source at real model shapes (hidden 4096, moe_intermediate 2048, E=256, top_k=6, IQ3_XXS):

**Arm 2** — H + released wheel:
```
ggml_supports_iq_mmq   -> ABSENT (ImportError)
_supports_iq_mmq        = False
IQ3_XXS in MMQ_QUANT_TYPES = False
MoE   M=1..16384       -> ggml_moe_a8_vec (per-token vec)
dense M>=17            -> dequantize
```

**Arm 3** — H + wheel built from H:
```

_supports_iq_mmq        = True
IQ3_XXS in MMQ_QUANT_TYPES = True
MoE   M=1,8,64,127     -> ggml_moe_a8_vec
      M=128            -> ggml_moe_a8 (batched MMQ)
      M=129,4096,16384 -> ggml_moe_a8
```

One scoping observation: issue #35019 named two fallbacks — dense projections and MoE experts. This PR closes the MoE one. The dense path still routes to `dequantize` for M >= 17 (dense MMQ gate is M <= 16), so prefill-sized batches never reach it. For this checkpoint that is nearly moot — all I-quant tensors are routed experts and all dense tensors are Q6_K/Q8_0/BF16 — but I want the issue not to be read as fully closed on the dense side.
